newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes get trashed, oversupply apparent.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes get trashed, oversupply apparent.

text.p: North Sea crude premiums got trashed on Tuesday with a cargo of November loading Brent crude trading 37 cents below Monday's traded level.

A November 5-7 Brent cargo sold at December -43 cents. This was followed by a November 10-12 Brent moving at December -38 cents. Of the three November 13-15 cargoes to turn wet today, two were subject to five o'clocking and one was kept.
Most traders expected this Brent deal to be the bottom of the market, but felt the other sweet North Sea grades had further to fall.

"This should be the low but we may stay here for another week. The fundamentals are bad. We need to see Brent or Oseberg move out of the area to save this market. The grades could lose another 10 cents," one refiner said.
A cargo of November 7-9 Statfjord was heard offered at dated Brent +10 cents after a bidder at this level moved back.
Ekofisk, Oseberg, Forties and Statfjord were expected to trade at low levels for the remaining first half November barrels before the end of the week, traders said.
"Everyone is stocked up here. The crude that is left has nowhere to go," one refiner said.

In the Mediterranean the situation was similar with Urals stacking up and refiners only looking at second half November barrels. West African grades were expected to soften. Qua Iboe was seen especially under pressure.
